title: Hypergumbo Behavior Map
description: Output schema for hypergumbo analysis. Auto-generated from Python dataclasses.

symbol_fingerprint_scheme.description: Identifier for the Symbol.fingerprint structural hashing scheme

generated_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when analysis was generated

analysis_incomplete.description: True if analysis was truncated or limited

analysis_runs.description: Provenance tracking for each analysis pass

features.description: Feature slice index entries (handler slices etc.); full slice content lives in per-slice side files

total_files.description: Node-distinct path count — number of distinct node.path values that survive analysis (INV-mozaf)

profile_files_sum.description: Legacy profile-language file-count sum, kept for introspection (over-counts vs node-distinct total_files)

reproducibility_context.description: L2 reproducibility metadata (INV-morag option B): direct dependencies + runtime identity, with an explicit not_captured disclosure of L3-L5 factors

captured.description: Recorded reproducibility inputs. Sub-keys tree_sitter_version / grammars appear only when tree-sitter is importable

not_captured.description: Factors that may affect reproducibility but are not recorded (transitive deps, OS, hardware)

implications.description: What diff-attribution level a consumer can expect from the captured fields alone

validation_report.description: Spec-vs-data validator output (ADR-0033): the triage surface for contract violations; never a build break

wired_checks.description: validator:F2 (WI-moriz) — the predicates actually wired into validate_ir, each mapped to the validator_class it contributes to. Makes a 0 count interpretable ('0 of these named checks', not '0 defects of any kind'); a defect class absent here is, by absence, not yet validated.

stable_id_stats.description: ADR-0035 §5 corpus stable_id population/collision/None-cohort disclosure over an all-Symbols denominator; always present so a clean non-null rate can never hide a None-cohort. Null on bare build_validation_report calls (unit tests).

sketch_precomputed.description: Precomputed sketch payload (vocabulary, centrality, readme description, config info). Optional; omitted when --no-sketch-precomputed. Each sub-field is nullable because small repos may not surface a README, license, or any centrality signal.

start_line.description: Starting line number (1-indexed); 0 reserved for synthetic boundary symbols (kind=external_symbol) which have no source location

end_line.description: Ending line number (1-indexed); 0 reserved for synthetic boundary symbols (kind=external_symbol) which have no source location

Symbol.description: A code symbol (function, class, method, etc.)

kind.description: Symbol type. Per ADR-0027, the canonical axiom is 'Symbol.kind names the source-language syntactic construct that the symbol represents.' The x-axis-of-values map below documents the canonical registry from packages/hypergumbo-core/src/hypergumbo_core/symbol_kinds.py::SYMBOL_KINDS. The schema enum is intentionally open (type: string without enum constraint) until ADR-0027 Phase 4b producer migrations land per-cluster — current production includes dynamic kind=f"ipc_{...}" emits at ipc.py:498 and phoenix_ipc.py:276 that produce values not in the static registry. The L3 producer-coherence linter (scripts/check-producer-axis-coherence) gates new literal additions against the registry; the open enum honestly reflects the producer-side leak the ADR is fixing.

language.description: Programming language of the host source file. Null for Class B synthetic stand-ins emitted by protocol linkers (ADR-0031) — those carry discovery_language + protocol_origin instead.

origin.description: Pass IDs that contributed to this symbol (INV-jidat)

stable_id.description: Structural identity hash within a (qualified_name, module_path) scope (ADR-0014 as amended by Phase 6 / INV-bazij): survives body edits, NOT rename or move

fingerprint.description: Structural content hash of the symbol's parse subtree (shape + identifiers + literals; whitespace/comment-invariant), prefixed with the scheme tag declared in symbol_fingerprint_scheme. Null when the span has no parseable content or no grammar is available.

is_test_file.description: True if the file holds test code (independent of tier)

is_example_file.description: True if the file is example/demo/sample/tutorial code

is_config_file.description: True if the file is a dependency/build manifest

is_generated_file.description: True if the file is generated code

is_exported.description: True if the symbol is part of the package's public API

lines_of_code.description: Number of source lines in the symbol body

signature.description: Function/method signature string, e.g., '(x: int, y: str) -> bool'

docstring.description: First-line summary of doc comment (truncated to 80 chars)

discovery_language.description: ADR-0031: host source language where a linker discovered the pattern that produced this Class B synthetic stand-in. Null for real-source declarations (language already carries that information).

protocol_origin.description: ADR-0031: protocol or framework family (kafka, websocket, grpc, database_query, ...) for Class B synthetic stand-ins. Catalog at protocol_origins.py. Null for real-source declarations.

display_label.description: ADR-0032: human-readable display string for synthetic linker stand-ins (e.g. "invoke('save_data')"). Consumers display it but never branch on it. Null for real-source declarations.

qualified_name.description: ADR-0032: fully-qualified name including ancestor containers, joined with the per-language separator declared in qualified_name_axis.py. Null when name already encodes the qualified form or no separator policy is declared.

origin.description: Pass IDs that contributed to this edge (INV-jidat)

is_resolved.description: Whether the dst symbol was resolved at analysis time. Per ADR-0028, this sibling field captures what the Cluster B `*_unresolved` evidence_type values previously smuggled into the inference label. Default True (the ~90% case); Phase 3 producers explicitly set False for the Cluster B fold targets.

dst_ref.description: Structured identity for the dst endpoint when it points at an external symbol (stdlib, dependency, unresolved external). Per WI-tihup, this is the canonical source of truth for external-target identity — the legacy `dst` string field is built from the same ExternalRef and stays populated alongside for back-compat with consumers that haven't migrated. None when dst points at an in-repo Symbol (whose `dst` field is a real Symbol ID).

derived_from.description: Symbol (or Edge) IDs the producer consumed to construct this Edge (INV-rukor). Populated by linkers; null for analyzer-originated edges.

evidence_type.description: Inference pathway by which the analyzer concluded this edge exists. Per ADR-0028, the canonical axiom is 'Edge.evidence_type names the inference pathway by which the analyzer concluded this edge exists.' The x-axis-of-values map documents the canonical registry from packages/hypergumbo-core/src/hypergumbo_core/evidence_types.py::EVIDENCE_TYPES. The schema enum is intentionally open (type: string without enum constraint) until Phase 4b producer migrations land per-cluster — current production includes dynamic f-string emits (websocket.py, di_resolution.py, inheritance.py) that produce values outside the static registry. The L3 producer-coherence linter gates literal additions; the open enum honestly reflects the producer-side leak the ADR is fixing.

AnalysisRun.description: Provenance tracking for an analysis pass

repo_fingerprint.description: Git state hash for cache invalidation

toolchain.description: Runtime that produced the analysis (python + tree-sitter/grammar versions when applicable)

config_fingerprint.description: sha256 fingerprint of the effective per-pass config

files_analyzed.description: Number of files analyzed by this pass

files_skipped.description: Number of files skipped by this pass

skipped_passes.description: Passes skipped at dispatch time or crashed mid-run, with reasons (a 'crashed: ' prefix marks a contained pass crash)

failed_files.description: Per-file failures recorded by this pass ({path, reason}; drained into limits.failed_files)

started_at.description: UTC timestamp when the pass started

pass_version.description: Code-hash of the pass module (compute_pass_version); distinct from `version` (the package version)

nodes_emitted.description: Number of Symbols this pass contributed (INV-gizik / INV-pitab); distinct from files_analyzed (a file count)

edges_emitted.description: Number of Edges this pass contributed (INV-gizik / INV-pitab); a pass with edges_emitted>0 must carry duration_ms>0

FailedFile.description: A file that failed during analysis

path.description: Repo-relative path of the failed file

analyzer.description: Pass ID of the analyzer that failed

ClassificationFailure.description: A file that failed supply chain classification

path.description: Path that could not be classified

AmbiguousPath.description: A file with ambiguous supply chain classification

assigned.description: Tier that was assigned despite ambiguity

classification_failures.description: Files that failed supply chain classification

Limits.description: Known gaps and limitations of this analysis — what was NOT captured, enabling honest downstream reporting

failed_files.description: Files that failed analysis ({path, reason, analyzer})

skipped_passes.description: Passes skipped at dispatch time or crashed mid-run, with reasons (a 'crashed: ' prefix marks a contained pass crash)

truncated_files.description: Files truncated or skipped due to size

partial_results_reason.description: Why results are partial, when they are

max_tier_applied.description: Max supply-chain tier filter applied, when any

max_files_per_analyzer.description: Per-analyzer file cap applied, when any

test_files_excluded.description: Present (true) when test files were excluded

analyzer_version.description: hypergumbo version string that produced this analysis

SliceQuery.description: The query that produced a feature slice (subset of SliceQuery fields that affect the stable feature id)

entrypoint.description: Symbol name, file path, or node ID the slice starts from

max_files.description: Max files included in the slice

max_tier.description: Max supply chain tier included, when set

exclude_imports.description: Present (true) when import edges were excluded

pass_through_kinds.description: Node kinds traversed but excluded from output

Feature.description: A feature slice index entry (spec §9 features[]): IDs + query + summary so consumers can discover slices via the behavior map alone and diff across commits via the stable id

entry_nodes.description: IDs of the entry point nodes

node_ids.description: Sorted IDs of all nodes in the slice

edge_ids.description: Sorted IDs of all edges in the slice

node_depths.description: Node ID → BFS depth, when recorded

node_tiers.description: Node ID → supply chain tier, when recorded

admission_stats.description: Per-rule dataflow edge-admission counters, when dataflow=True

id.description: Stable feature ID (sha256 of the canonical query JSON)

ValidationViolation.description: One structured spec-vs-data mismatch from the end-of-pipeline validator stage (ADR-0033)

validator_class.description: Which validator class emitted this (axis_conformance, writer_contract, cross_field, verdict_enum, id_format)

expected.description: Short description of what was expected

Entrypoint.description: A detected program entrypoint (main function, CLI verb, HTTP route, etc.). Produced by `detect_entrypoints()`.

symbol_id.description: ID of the Symbol that is the entrypoint

kind.description: Entrypoint category — e.g. main_function, cli_command, http_route, framework_handler

UsageContext.description: Concept-tagged usage site (per ADR-0003-ext usage_context_patterns) — e.g. a Flask `@app.route` call or a Django ORM filter.

id.description: Stable hash ID for this usage site

context_name.description: Name of the function/decorator/sentinel at this site (e.g. 'Route', 'session.query')

kind.description: Usage kind — call, data_value, export, macro

path.description: Source file path (relative to repo root)

position.description: Position descriptor — e.g. args[0], view_func, default (per ADR-0003-ext positional vocabulary)

symbol_ref.description: Resolved Symbol ID if available, otherwise null

metadata.description: Per-pattern metadata payload (e.g. {route_path, methods, view_name} for a Flask route)

UsagePatternSpec.description: Specification for matching usage contexts (call-based frameworks)

kind.description: Regex pattern to match context kind (call, data_value, export, macro)

name.description: Regex pattern to match context_name (function called, var defined, etc.)

position.description: Regex pattern to match position (args[1], :get, default, etc.)

Pattern.description: A pattern to match against symbol metadata or usage contexts

concept.description: The concept type this pattern identifies (route, model, task, etc.)

decorator.description: Regex pattern to match against decorator names

base_class.description: Regex pattern to match against base class names

parent_base_class.description: Regex pattern to match parent class's base classes (for methods)

method_name.description: Regex pattern to match method name (last part of qualified name)

symbol_name.description: Regex pattern to match symbol name directly

language.description: Regex pattern to filter by symbol's language

annotation.description: Regex pattern to match against Java annotations

parameter_type.description: Regex pattern to match against parameter types

symbol_kind.description: Regex pattern to match against symbol kind field

extract_path.description: JSONPath-like expression to extract route path from metadata

extract_method.description: How to derive HTTP method (decorator_suffix, kwargs.methods, etc.)

prefix_from_parent.description: Concept name to look up on parent class for path prefix (v1.3.x)

usage.description: UsagePatternSpec for matching against UsageContext records

extract.description: Dict of extraction expressions for usage-based patterns

linkers.description: Linkers that should be activated when this framework is detected
